page: Microsoft Azure EC32as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 x86_64 processor. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The memory subsystem delivers 192.0 GB of RAM, equating to 6.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware cache provisioning includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Cryptographic execution is supported via hardware AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, while vector processing relies on standard AVX instructions. Running under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance includes no local storage or GPUs, requiring remote networked storage volumes.

Performance testing places the instance in the average band across standardized suites. The 32 vCPUs achieve a PassMark CPU score of 33294.69 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 34367.38, complemented by a single-core stress-ng rating of 2334.26. In Geekbench testing, the server scores 1401.0 in single-core and 11035.0 in multi-core routines, with subtests reaching 21849.0 for Clang compilation and 30807.0 for ray tracing. The memory architecture registers a PassMark memory score of 2211.86 and drives 29.05 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, alongside a PassMark database score of 11945.07.

The absence of local disks necessitates relying on remote storage, which introduces latency considerations for intensive I/O operations compared to systems with local NVMe. However, the generous 192.0 GB memory footprint paired with dedicated AMD EPYC cores provides a stable environment for memory-heavy deployments. The server aligns with workloads such as in-memory caching platforms, enterprise relational databases, medium-scale data analytics pipelines, and general enterprise applications requiring substantial memory allocation per thread.
